findings.defect: Residual of previous item 4. A plate still adds 14 % of whatever is behind it, so every hard scene edge is a hard edge inside the plate. On the lit lunar surface the landing-target panel is (15, 21, 29) above the horizon and (49, 55, 64) below it: a 34-level step, 1 px wide, cutting through the row "TRACK · ARRIVAL none". On the pad the horizon cuts the LAUNCH panel's last row ((42, 51, 62) above, (26, 37, 49) below), and the white rocket is a visible band behind the primary altitude read-out ((38, 48, 63) plate, (44, 50, 60) and (33, 39, 49) on the rocket's lit and shaded sides). In warp-refused the same rocket band runs behind the toast text. Stage tiles that straddle the horizon are two-toned. Over space, stars are faintly visible between rows. Label contrast itself is fine everywhere.
findings.realReference: A plate over a high-contrast edge needs either enough opacity that the edge falls to a few levels, or a blurred and darkened backdrop (frosted glass); shipped flight HUDs do one or the other (KSP 1 instrument plates are opaque), so a horizon never shows as a sharp line through a text row. The sunlit-regolith-to-black-sky horizon of the Moon (C:dev able-space-gameoutqaefmoon-surface) is the highest-contrast edge in the game and will cross the left column for the whole descent.
findings.likelyCause: The plate fills are rgba(17, 24, 34, 0.86) and rgba(22, 30, 42, 0.87) with no backdrop treatment (`--bg`, `--bg-top` in C:\dev\fable-space-game\src\ui\hud\hudStyles.ts lines 17-18, the first now read from `UI_COLORS.panel` in C:\dev\fable-space-game\src\core\ui\theme.ts). A white-to-black edge behind a plate therefore survives as 0.14 x 240 = 34 levels.
findings.fixDirection: Raise the plate alpha to 0.96 or more (the worst step drops under 10 levels), or add `backdrop-filter: blur()` of at least 12 px if its GPU cost at 4K fits the 0.5 ms HUD budget (measure it). Extend the near-white spec: sample each plate that straddles the horizon in bright-lunarSurface and assert its fill varies by less than about 8 levels.

findings.defect: At a healthy 80 % heat shield the ABLATOR gauge is filled bright warning red from 0 to the 30 % redline and cyan above it. The red block is the most saturated element on the page and reads as an alarm at a nominal reading: the same fault class as previous item 1 (colour says "limit" when nothing is wrong). The three places that show this quantity disagree: the HUD resources bar is green, the HUD entry panel's heat-shield bar is cyan, and the MFD bar is red and cyan. The row beside the gauge prints "ABLATOR 80 %" in the normal tone.
findings.realReference: Quantity gauges where low is bad (propellant and consumable bars on real spacecraft displays, KSP resource bars) draw the whole fill in the colour of the zone the reading is in and turn red only once the level is below the limit. The limit zone is a mark on the scale, not part of the fill.
findings.likelyCause: `drawBarGauge` in C:\dev\fable-space-game\src\ui\mfd\mfdPainter.ts lines 959-973 paints "the fill in the zone colour of each part": every zone below the reading is filled at full strength in its own colour. That is right for g load and temperature, whose zones stack upward from green. The ablator's zones are `[[0.3, COLORS.warning], [1, COLORS.accent]]` (lines 1030-1038), so the lowest 30 % is red whenever any ablator is left.
findings.fixDirection: Give `GaugeSpec` a low-is-bad flag. For those gauges colour the whole fill by the zone of the current value (accent above the redline, warning only below it) and keep the red zone as the faint track tint under the redline. Use one colour for the ablator on the HUD bars and the MFD. Add a painter test: at ablatorFraction 0.8 no pixel of the ablator bar is warning red.

findings.view: C:\dev\fable-space-game\out\screens\flight-ui\mfd-pages-4k.png and mfd-pages-native.png (FLT page, lunar orbit); C:\dev\fable-space-game\out\screens\flight-ui\mfd-pages-hover-4k.png (FLT page)
findings.defect: Clipped and colliding scale text on the flight page. (a) Speed tape: "1700" is cut in half by the tape's top edge and the top of "1640" pokes out above the black read-out box; altitude tape: "104" and "96" are cut at the top and bottom edges. (b) V/S scale: the tick at 100 runs into the "1" of "100" on both sides of zero, so the climb side reads "-100". (c) Heading tape: "05" is cut to "5" at the left end and "12" touches the right end. (d) Pitch ladder: the 25-degree rungs lie exactly on the ladder's clip circle and remain as thin lens-shaped slivers at the top and bottom of the ladder, in every FLT picture.
findings.realReference: Glass-cockpit tapes (Orion, Crew Dragon, airliner primary flight displays) mask scale numerals completely behind the read-out window and fade or drop them at the tape ends; tick labels never touch their ticks.
findings.likelyCause: C:\dev\fable-space-game\src\ui\mfd\mfdPainter.ts: `drawTape` (lines 387-446) clips only to the tape rectangle and draws every label within value +- span, then draws the read-out box (height 0.06 of the page) over them without skipping labels it half covers. `drawVsi` (lines 460-466) draws ticks from x to x + 0.3 tw and right-aligns labels at x + 0.94 tw, which a three-character label overruns. `drawAdi` (lines 570-578) draws rungs while |y| <= 1.05 x ladderR inside a clip of radius ladderR.
findings.fixDirection: Skip a tape label when its box crosses a tape end or lies within half the read-out box plus half a line of the centre, or fade labels with a gradient mask at the ends. Shorten the V/S ticks to about 0.15 tw or left-align the labels after the tick. Skip ladder rungs with |y| > ladderR minus the line width, and heading labels closer than half their width to the ends.

findings.defect: Nose-up, the MFD attitude indicator is an empty disc: one flat navy (15, 52, 102) over about 85 % of its area (the sky gradient ends 100 px below the top at 4K), no horizon, no zenith mark, and two rungs whose numerals read upside down ("0L", "08"). The velocity marker is hidden under the aircraft symbol. Beside the HUD ball, which shows the same attitude with a pole ring and numeral spokes, it looks unlit and unfinished. This is the first and last attitude of every mission.
findings.realReference: The Apollo FDAI in C:\dev\fable-space-game\out\qa\ref\cockpit-interiors\apollo11-columbia-panel.jpg carries distinct pole markings, so straight up is a recognisable picture. 2-D attitude displays that must cover +-90 degrees draw a zenith and nadir symbol on the ladder.
findings.likelyCause: `drawAdi` in C:\dev\fable-space-game\src\ui\mfd\mfdPainter.ts lines 549-554: the sky is a linear gradient from the horizon to 2.4 r above it, clamped beyond. At pitch 90 the horizon is 2.88 r away (ladderR / 25 px per degree), so only the clamped end colour is on the disc. The ladder has no symbol at +-90.
findings.fixDirection: Add zenith and nadir symbols to the ladder (a ring or star at +-90). When the horizon is off the disc, grade the fill about the pole (a radial gradient centred on the 90-degree point) so the disc is never one flat colour. Draw the velocity marker over the aircraft symbol's open centre.

findings.defect: Low readings in the G tube are not a column. At 1.00 g the fill is a green egg sitting in the tube (rounded fill top inside the tube's rounded bottom). At 0.17 g the whole fill is the white highlight cap: a pale 4 px lens with no green in it. The scale numerals (0 / 4 / 8 / 12 and 0 / 50 / 100) are 5 px tall at 720p, and the top numeral sits about 4 px under the value, so "0 %" over "100" reads as one block.
findings.realReference: Vertical tape gauges (the tapes on the Apollo panel in C:\dev\fable-space-game\out\qa\ref\cockpit-interiors\apollo11-columbia-panel.jpg, Shuttle MEDS tapes) have a flat fill top or a pointer, and scale numerals as large as the captions.
findings.likelyCause: C:\dev\fable-space-game\src\ui\hud\hudStyles.ts lines 315-321: `.win` has a 1.1u top radius and a 0.35u-high cap at 55 % white (`.win::after`); any fill shorter than the tube's 1.3u end radius is also clipped by the round end. `.nums` is 0.6em.
findings.fixDirection: Give the tube square ends, or the fill a flat top with a 1 px lighter line. Limit the cap to a third of the fill height. Raise the numerals to 0.72em or more and move the top numeral clear of the value row.
